text.p: Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (PICIC) jumped 1.50 rupees, or 30 percent, to 6.50 on reports that the new caretaker government planned to merge it with other state-run financial institutions, dealers said.
A turnover of 3,500 shares of the stock had been recorded at the Karachi bourse by midsession.
"Yesterday the stock price tumbled on news reports that the government planned to liquidate PICIC. But now there is news of its merger which has pushed its price up," dealer Sajjad Mankani said.

Shahid Javed Burki, finance and economic affairs adviser to the new caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid, said on Saturday that several state-owned financial institutions, including PICIC, would be "abolished, consolidated or reformed".
The Finance Ministry, of which Burki took charge on Friday, said on Sunday that it planned to restructure or merge certain state-owned financial institutions, but not scrap them.
The statement from the Finance Ministry did not say specifically that PICIC would be merged.
PICIC is 55.44 percent owned by the private sector.

The Finance Ministry said that government-owned corporations, such as State Life Insurance Corporation, which hold the rest of the equity might be asked to give up their holdings in PICIC to make it more efficient and independent.
